instruction: Replace the account "anonym-x2024@outlook.com" with a new account "newuser2024@gmail.com".

metadata.explanation: Task requires removing one account and adding a different account. Evaluator uses existing check_csv metric to verify the new account exists and the old account has been removed. No custom functions needed - reuses existing check_csv from general.py.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic correctly verifies BOTH requirements: new account exists (expect) and old account removed (unexpect)
Complete coverage of instruction - checks account replacement comprehensively
Correct parameter handling for type='rule': metric receives rules dict directly, not nested structure
Appropriate postconfig: firefox_decrypt.py extracts Thunderbird account credentials to CSV format for verification
Correct data flow: postconfig extracts state → get_cache_file retrieves CSV → check_csv verifies expect/unexpect rules
check_csv logic is sound: iterates through CSV records, matches expect rules (all must match) and unexpect rules (none should match)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor concern: Assumes firefox_decrypt.py outputs CSV with 'user' column header. If the tool uses different column names (e.g., 'username', 'email', 'account'), verification will fail. Consider verifying the actual CSV output format from firefox_decrypt.py or adding documentation about the expected CSV schema.
Consider adding error handling documentation for cases where firefox_decrypt.py might fail in non-interactive mode (-n flag) or if the Thunderbird profile is locked/corrupted
